## Why

The v1.0.7 branch dry-run (run 34729832126, `release` job, step "CHANGELOG
discipline — resolve external-contributor credits") resolved the WRONG pull
request for essentially every fragment: unrelated fragments collapsed onto the
same few recent merge numbers. `changelog/cellctl-cockpit-select.md` resolved to
#913, but its adding commit is `c2ee74ef feat(cellctl): … (#917)` — a squash
merge sitting directly on main.

The cause is the resolution ORDER in `aggregate.py`'s `credits` subcommand. It
read the ancestry-path merges FIRST and took the oldest one unconditionally:

- a SQUASH landing has no merge that brought it in, so the resolver credited it
  to whatever unrelated pull request merged above it;
- a fragment that never landed on a pull request at all did the same, instead of
  printing `unresolved`;

## Summary

Sub-split (a) of the statusgen/26 brief: `statusgen` adopts the shared perf-v3 recorder, on top of the perf-v2 record that medici-finance/assay#3745 landed on main.

- **Selected profile → perf-v3.** With `ASSAY_TELEMETRY=1` and a `tool` or `workflow` profile selected (`ASSAY_PERF_PROFILE` or `--perf-profile`), each process writes one perf-v3 process-summary record through `perfrec` (the same writer, day files, retention and install id as the desk tools).
- **No profile → perf-v2, unchanged.** With the switch on and no profile (unset, `off`, or invalid), statusgen writes main's perf-v2 record exactly as before: its stage roster, its `http` counter and its boundary do not move. Switch off creates nothing.
- **Two sessions, never mixed.** The perf-v2 session is begun at package initialisation, before any flag is parsed; when a profile is selected only its record is dropped. The perf-v3 session (`perfV3Session`, roster `perfV3Phases`) is begun once the context resolves. Both start at the shared process-init mark and end at the exit wrapper.
- **perf-v3 phase roster** `discover`, `parse`, `evaluate`, `render`, `write`, `deskread`. Phases are exclusive (entering a nested phase pauses its parent), so `phaseOverlap` is always false and `n` counts segments. `evaluate` is the residue between a clean flag parse and exit. Seams: stream/archive discovery in `load.go`; README/brief/findings parsing in `parse.go`, `brieffile.go` and `load.go`; output emit and the gate-scores/next-up JSON in `main.go` and `dispatchqueue.go`; the STATUS write; and both deskread child starts in `forgeread.go`. In `main.go` the render seam carries both the v2 stage call and the v3 phase call.
- **Flag binding.** The eight `--perf-*` flags are registered on statusgen's own flag set (statusgen may not import the desk adapter) and fed to `perfrec.ResolveContext` exactly as the flag parser accepted them. A flag overrides its environment variable, an empty flag clears it, and malformed values become `invalid` coverage that never changes output or exit.
- **deskread parent link.** Both deskread child starts time the child's wait as the `deskread` phase. When recording, they hand the child this run's context as `--perf-*` flags on its own argv, after the read kind. `perfrec.ContextEnv` (fed no inherited environment) decides what is forwarded:
  - workflow: session, agent, role and work, with this invocation as `parentInvocationId`;
  - tool: the profile alone;
  - no profile: `--perf-profile=off`.
- **Version gate.** The flags are passed only when the resolved `deskread` lists every one of them in its `--help`. The probe runs once per process, with an empty environment, a 15s bound and a `WaitDelay`, and it runs before the `deskread` phase opens, so the phase times only the child. An older `deskread`, which would refuse an unknown flag, gets none, so output and exit never change. The parent records no request observation (`requestCoverage: missing`); the child owns its provider requests.
- `docs/telemetry.md`: statusgen perf-v3 section (profile selection; perf-v2 kept when no profile; phase roster and segment semantics; shared boundary; the deskread link, its version gate and its coverage gap; a note that the context on the child's argv is visible to local users who can list processes and holds only validated, non-credential values; how `deskperf report` reads these records; and the resolver-20 note).

## What changes

- **Phases.** `run()` is split into fixed, non-overlapping stages: `parse`, `lint`, `briefs`, `ordering`, `evidence`, `links`, `claims`, `view`, `render`, `write`, `corroborate`.
  - The record lists them in **roster order**, which is not always the order a run enters them: the view build is entered before the claim read and resumed after it, but `claims` is listed before `view`.
  - A stage entered more than once collects into one entry, and its `n` counts the entries. That covers one `run()` per root, the source lint resumed around its named sub-stages, and the view build on both sides of the claim read.
  - `briefs`, `ordering` and `evidence` are split out of `lint` because each took more than ~5% of a full `--lint` of this repository. Every other check stays inside `lint`. `evidence` runs only on a root with a `.git`.
  - `--corroborate` is timed as its own stage.
- **`http` counter.** Every direct HTTP attempt at statusgen's forge seams is counted at the call, immediately before the client's `Do`. A retry, a 304 and a transport failure each count once. A redirect the client follows inside one `Do` is part of that attempt and is not counted again. The seams are:
  - the GitHub REST client
  - the claim-decay GraphQL post
  - the GitLab MR page read
  - the telemetry sender (its endpoint is empty in shipped builds)

  Because it is counted at the call, the counter is MEASURED even when it is 0.
- **Unavailable counters.** `subprocess` and the other counters are listed as unavailable. statusgen's many `gh`/`git` child processes have no shared seam to count.
- **sourceSHA.** It is read in exactly one helper, `perfSourceStamp()`. Today that returns the build version, so a release tag records `unpinned` (the shared writer keeps only a commit-shaped stamp).
- **Docs.** `docs/telemetry.md` and `perfrec/README.md` say statusgen writes perf-v2, list its phases, and say that phases are in roster order and do not sum to `wallMs`. Every remaining statement in the tree that said statusgen writes perf-v1 is corrected: the statusgen section of `docs/telemetry.md` (now: one perf-v2 record, `http` measured, `subprocess` unavailable), `tools/desk/README.md`, the `perfrec/schema.go` package comment, and three test comments. Merge the sibling change that stamps release binaries with their source commit **first**. That change is not open as a PR yet; its number will be added here when it is. Implements brief 27. Stacked on the brief's own PR (merged in, so this branch carries the
board row it has to flip); the brief's diff is the first commit here and is reviewed there.

## Measured, back to back, same host and roster, structurally identical output

Each pair below is the `origin/main` binary and this branch's binary run one after the other
in the same window, against the same ten-repo roster and four stream roots. The output of
every pair was compared field by field: identical except the clock-derived fields (`asOf`,
`openAge`, `daysStalled`), which move between two runs seconds apart.

| verb | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stalled` | 84.82 s | 12.63 s | 6.7× |
| `prs` | 19.82 s | 6.63 s | 3.0× |
| `throughput` | 47.65 s | 29.10 s | 1.6× |

policy-drift probe, which rode inside it as a ten-deep serial chain of forge reads next to an
idle pool. It is also the verb that matters most: 8,328 of 9,614 recorded `deskboard`
invocations on this host, 86.6%.

   `prs` and the drift probe per repo; `stalled` per repo AND, inside each repo's worker, per
   PR — the same nesting `actions` has run since it was pooled, so the bound on concurrent
   forge reads is the one the suite already operates at, not a new one. Fail-closed is
   preserved everywhere it existed and deliberately NOT introduced where it did not: the drift
   probe still never kills the board, and its call site says so.
2. **One root resolution, and the roots read concurrently.** `dispatch` and `awaiting` each
   carried an identical five-step preamble and then walked their roots serially; a
   `throughput` run therefore did all of it twice. Both now go through `resolveRootsOnce` and
   `runPerRoot` (bound 4, deliberately its own number — this is a local subprocess per root,
   not a forge read, so it must not be re-tuned by a change made for a forge reason).
3. **`throughput` derives its depths from that one resolution** plus one `actions` sweep.
   Blind stays blind, and the one new way to break it is closed and tested: a failed shared
   resolution blinds BOTH stages it fed, each naming it, so no reader is left thinking one
   stage's depth is real because the other's was.
4. **The drift self-check resolves the per-platform pin name.** A consumer pinning
   `desk-tools-<os>-<arch>` — the line the published pin contract tells them to pin — got a
   permanent could-not-check reported as STALE. Fixed with a second EXACT lookup, never a
   looser match: the trailing-space prefix rule is a control and is untouched, and the bare
   line still wins when both are present.
5. **`deskflip` cheapest gate first, and the rollup read once.** See the correction below for
   what the ordering actually became and why. The check rollup at head was fetched twice in
   one run by two conditions; it is now fetched once, with each condition still reporting a
   failure under its own name.

   1,611 refusals measured over 32 days) are body-schema refusals its own `--dry-run` would
   have caught, and neither mentioned it.

   `flag.ErrHelp` recognition at the parse. Retrofitted into the six verbs that actually
   produced rows.

The cost-ordering the dispatch note asked for puts `checks-green` fourth. Implementing it
reddens two tests in `tools/desk/cmd/deskflip/checkonlycr_test.go` whose comments record the
opposite rule with its reasoning: when a standing CHANGES_REQUESTED claims the check-only
exemption, the exemption must decide BEFORE `checks-green`, or an operator rejected for a
reason that was never about CI is sent to the CI gate to look for it. One of the two also
changes exit code (a still-running cited run becomes a pending rollup, 6, instead of a
rejected exemption claim, 5).

than a safety one — but it is a deliberately recorded decision and a performance brief does
not get to overturn it quietly. So the ordering taken is the one that does not collide with
it: `mergeable` up from seventh to fourth (it costs NO forge read — it reads a field the PR
document read already populated), `model-floor` down from fourth to seventh (it buys a
paginated label-event timeline). `reviewer-approved` keeps its place ahead of `checks-green`,
and since both now read one memoized rollup the cost argument for swapping them has largely
evaporated anyway. Whether the exemption's precedence should be revisited is left open and
named in the brief rather than resolved here.

`mergeable` is not re-read (it comes from the PR payload, which made it a BETTER reordering

A `mergeable` refusal: ONE forge read, the PR document, down from four — asserted by counting
the stub's requests, not by trusting the order. A `checks-green` refusal: three, down from
four; the one dropped is the paginated timeline.

at a flag that is not there would be worse than saying nothing. `deskpost`'s two largest
classes do carry the hint. Everything else in the DoD is met and measured, and the remaining
work is one bounded flag plus its two call sites.
